[h1]Overall Rating: 6/10[/h1]

[b]Pro’s:[/b]
- Impressive gunplay with satisfying sounds and feels.
- Lots of Enemy types to test players
- Hidden secrets to find, including Loot stashes that have random locations.
- Perk system is well executed.
- Almost all the classes feel different and impact the overall gameplay experience in a unique way.
- Final Boss is great and the level design in the later missions of the game are great. Large organic open spaces contrast well with the narrow, industrial corridors of the earlier campaigns.
- Cooperative play is very polished and the game’s missions are built around Coop itself.
- Interesting lore once you actually can be bothered to read into it as the game doesn't explain most of it. There is a LOT to read though!
- Final Mission in the [i]base game is very intense[/i] and has a sweat inducing ending. Unfortunately there is no final boss battle, like wtf?
- Synthetic Enemies act very differently to Xenos and require very different strategies. (Headshots and Electro Turret Emplacements). This is great as it requires players to stay on their toes and plan firefights accordingly.

[b]Con’s:[/b]
- Animations feel stiff and lack fluidity. Sprinting is pretty slow overall and you can only roll 3 times before you completely drain your stamina bar.
- Lobby music is extremely repetitive and lacks additional tracks
- Prowlers are just garbage enemies as their only purpose is to keep players alert when entering corridors and turning corners, which on its own sounds fine, however at their core, they are just a Hunter from L4D2 with an annoying quick time event. Unoriginal and tiresome in my opinion.
-During the later missions, Elite enemies like the Warrior and Crusher spawn too rapidly to keep up with. The area can very quickly fill up with fodder enemies while you and your team mates prioritise the larger enemies. The point here is that it feels like the game will just spawn a larger number of enemies than you are used to just to slow progress and create a sense of artifical difficulty. When the area is completely filled with enemies and both team mates are downed, the last thing I am thinking is strategy, it all goes out the window as its just too frantic. Sure the stress can make it fun at times, but 90% of the time I have not survived the remaining onslaught..
- No Final Boss Battle in the base game. Just a timed escape section which feels very cinematic, but lacks a climax which after all the close quarters fighting during the level is a major disappointment.
- 3 Player Coop limit was a very strange Idea and I am not sure why this was chosen. I'm sure there is a good reason but It feels weird.
- Bots perform terribly on anything over standard difficulty. (Intense, Extreme and Insane)
- On Intense difficulty and Above, enemies feel gradually more and more bullet spongy, their AI is unchanged, spawns change slightly but the main spike in each difficulty level is how much damage the enemies can take. This is incredibly lazy in my opinion and far too many games change minimal mechanics to create harder difficulties.
- Some Firefights with Synths feel unbalanced and go on for far too long. 
- Miniboss - Enemies like the [spoiler]Crusher and Praetorian[/spoiler] don't have very clear weak points and when they charge at you, their large armoured head block you from hitting weak points anyway…
- No text chat or voice chat. SERIOUSLY, THIS IS A VERY STRATEGIC COOPERATIVE GAME [b]WITHOUT[/b] MEANS TO COMMUNICATE!
- Dead playerbase, nuff said
- 4 different campaigns with 3 levels each, totalling 12 separate Missions that each take 20 to 25 minutes each. Doing the math we find that (On average) the game will take 180 to 250 minutes. This is just the mission time though. Customizing your perks, classes and guns will add maybe 5 minutes between missions but ultimately this game is criminally short. It's definitely [i]not worth full price at its current length[/i].
- Synth Heavies are the tankiest enemies I've seen in a game for a very long time. I feel like changing my perks and attachments only goes so far when It takes multiple clips to down enemies like the Synth Warden, Synth Heavy,  Xeno Crusher and even the Xeno Drone!
- The Stalker enemy (Pathogen Heavy) is literally only in one or two of the base game missions. It's a great enemy with an ability to naturally camouflage temporarily and flank your team! I loved this enemy design but barely got enough time to appreciate how unique it was..
- Emotes, Weapon Decals and even some of the Hats ruin the tone of the game and can destroy your immersion to see a teammate doing a chicken dance after a massive battle. I get that it adds customisation to the game but it just doesn't suit the tone at all.
- No server browser
- The Pathogen expansion adds maybe an hour of new content. IMO It is worth maybe $8 NZD for the content it brings. Very disappointing. Great Lore and epic ending, but cmon...
- Flamethrowers are iconic and all, but they block your view severely when someone is firing one. Their friendly fire is also insane as they have a massive spread..
-No First person mode implemented. Real missed opportunity for the devs here.
- Can't join someone's game that has already started a mission. Why not??
-  Far too many weapons for my liking. Could be less of em but more unique. The attachments and guns seem to blend together once you unlock a good bunch of them.
- Lip syncing is either broken or not implemented when talking to NPCs in the Lobby. (IN A 2022 GAME

Lots of cons yes, but somehow, the game is [i]still[/i] a solid Cooperative Experience.
If you love this genre of games, then I highly recommend the following Intense cooperative shooters:

I love this game, but the terrible community and peer to peer matchmaking ruins it. The community is cancer. People will join horde mode and leave after round 1 for no apparent reason. If that player happens to be the host, then the match ends. You're better off playing with bots, honestly. The amount of quitters, or people with third world internet connection is unreal. Also, you will play with console players almost exclusively. It's frustrating to wait long periods of time to find players, only for them to quit or lag out. The game is extremely fun, however, and I wish I could leave this a mixed review.
